#### 1. amyloidosis, hereditary systemic 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.475)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-114608)

**Proposed mechanism:** VWF (HGNC:12172) —DISRUPTS→ von Willebrand factor multimerization and function (GO:0007542); von Willebrand factor multimerization and function (GO:0007542) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding (HP:00114070); APOA1 (HGNC:557) —DISRUPTS→ Lipoprotein metabolism (GO:0006629); Lipoprotein metabolism (GO:0006629) —DECREASES→ Apolipoprotein A-I containing lipoproteins (GO:0034377); Apolipoprotein A-I containing lipoproteins (GO:0034377) —LEADS_TO→ Amyloidosis (HP:0002668). Loss-of-function mutations in VWF lead to impaired VWF multimerization and function, resulting in bleeding diathesis characteristic of von Willebrand disease type 3. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in APOA1 disrupt normal lipoprotein metabolism, leading to the accumulation of amyloidogenic proteins and subsequent amyloidosis.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in VWF are found to be gain-of-function or dominant-negative, or if mutations in APOA1 are found to be gain-of-function or dominant-negative, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in VWF or APOA1 with a minor allele frequency > 0.001 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis and distinct functional consequences of VWF and APOA1 mutations can inform therapeutic strategies for bleeding disorders and amyloidosis, potentially identifying common pathways for intervention.

Loss-of-function mutations in VWF (von Willebrand disease 3) and ITGA2B (platelet-type bleeding disorder 16) both impair platelet function and the coagulation cascade, converging on a severe bleeding tendency.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a VWF or ITGA2B variant with a minor allele frequency >0.01 in gnomAD that perfectly segregates with either disease would challenge the pathogenicity of the proposed LoF mechanism. _(variant: rs121918575)_
